content.title: Queens College - Degree Programs, Accreditation, Application, Tuition & Financial Aid
content.text: Undergraduate & Graduate Programs at Queens College Queens College appears in our ranking of 60 Great Value Colleges for Music Majors (Undergraduate). Academic programs at Queens College are offered within four divisions that include the Arts & Humanities, Mathematics & the Natural Sciences, Education, and the Social Sciences. There are more than 170 areas of study available at Queens College, which also runs an honors program and provides day and evening classes for its students. Within the Division of Arts & Humanities, students may study music, art, foreign languages, literature, theater, English, film, linguistics, communication, and media studies. Students interested in music may enroll in classes offered by the Aaron Copland School of Music. Students who want to enroll in programs from the Division of Education will choose from three major areas of study that include Educational & Community Programs, Secondary Education & Youth Services, and Elementary & Early Childhood Education. Meanwhile, students who want to study math or natural science will take classes from the Division of Mathematics & the Natural Sciences. Areas of study available include biology, computer science, earth & environmental science, mathematics, and physics, as well as other related programs. Students may also have an interest in the Science Teacher Careers Office if they want to become teachers of natural science. The final division at Queens College is the Division of Social Sciences, which features degrees on topics like accounting, anthropology, journalism, and religious studies. Several degrees within this division deal with different cultures around the world, and students can enroll in programs in Irish Studies, Byzantine & Modern Greek Studies, Africana Studies, and Latin American & Latino Studies. One of the unique features of classes at Queens College is the Adult Collegiate Education program, which offers accelerated degree programs in which adults and students above the age of 25 can enroll. The college also has a Professional & Continuing Studies unit for students interested in certificate programs and professional development and enrichment classes. Students who want to study online at Queens College will have the choice of several career training programs offered within a partnership between the college and the Emerging Technologies Institute. Students can expand upon their current skill-sets or enroll in classes offering instruction on entirely new topics. The college offers several information technology certifications including those leading to Microsoft Certified Solutions Associate, MCSA Windows Server 2016, and Internetworking and Telecommunications Skills. Other topics available for study online include human resources, communication skills, leadership, finance, accounting, and customer service. In addition to certifications, the college also offers one- and two-year programs in Business Office Information Systems, Computer Network Administration, Management & Leadership, Web Design & Software Development, and a handful of other areas. About Queens College Queens College is part of the City University of New York and offers classes on a campus of 80 acres in Flushing, Queens, which is one of the boroughs of New York City. The school was established in 1937 with a motto of “We Learn So That We May Serve.” The school’s official colors are blue and silver and the athletic teams play as the Knights in their NCAA Division II games. The college sits on land that was once a single-room schoolhouse called Jamaica Academy, and Queens College was meant to be a free college for the citizens of Queens. In the 1970s, the administrative leaders of the City College of New York decided to adopt an open admissions policy for applicants who were residents of New York as a way to boost the number of minority students attending college. The college would revoke its free tuition policy in the mid-1970s. Queens College Accreditation Details Regional accreditation for Queens College is given by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education, which accredits schools throughout New York and neighboring states like Pennsylvania. The New York State Department of Education also accredits Queens College to operate in the state for the purpose of granting degrees. Programs offered throughout the college also hold specialized or programmatic accreditations. Some of the accrediting agencies that have granted approval to programs at the college include the Council for the Accreditation of Education Preparation, the American Psychological Association, Commission on Accreditation, and the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology. Additional accreditation comes from the American Association of Family & Consumer Sciences and the American Library Association. Queens College Application Requirements First-year applicants to Queens College must meet three criteria to gain acceptance to the school. Those standards include having an average GPA of 80 or higher in high school and an SAT score of at least 1130 on the critical reading and math sections. Alternatively, students can take the ACT and score a 22 or higher in the math and English sections. Applicants must also complete four years of English, three years of math, and other recommended classes. Meanwhile, students who want to enroll in graduate school will need to have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college and be able to demonstrate adequate preparation for study in graduate school. Tuition and Financial Aid Tuition for students at Queens College is $3,365 per semester for New York State residents and $600 per credit for out-of-state residents and international students. Part-time students in undergraduate classes will pay $295 per credit, and out-of-state students will pay $600 per credit for half-time study. Non-degree students will pay $430 per credit if they’re from New York State or $890 per credit if they’re from out-of-state. Graduate students who want to attend Queens College will pay $5,385 per semester if they’re from New York State or $830 per credit if they’re from out-of-state. Graduate students who enroll in fewer than 12 credits will pay $455 per credit for in-state tuition or $830 per credit for out-of-state tuition. Students can also enroll in classes as non-degree students for the same rate. Students may receive a combination of grants, loans, Work-Study awards, and scholarships when they attend Queens College. Students must submit their FAFSA form to qualify for federal student aid and may need to submit individual applications for each available scholarship. Some of the federal grants a student may receive when they apply for financial aid include Federal Pell Grants, TEACH Grants, and Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grants. Students may speak with the Office of Financial Aid Services at Queens College for more information on available student aid.
